transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in?

Well, thanks for fitting me in. Honestly, it took a bit of doing to finally get me in here. I’m out on the road a lot—I drive trucks, deliver freight, you know how it is. You gotta be sharp out there, keep your eyes on the road and your mind on the schedule. 

But... well, over these past few months, it’s like my brain just won’t stay in its lane. I’m driving, and suddenly my mind is just jumping to absolutely everything. Every single little chirp on the CB radio, every neon fuel price sign I pass on the interstate, or just... I don’t know, some completely new idea pops into my head out of nowhere and I'm just off to the races thinking about it. 

And the thing is, normally, I’m the guy who never misses a thing. I pride myself on being on top of it, checking the manifest twice, making sure everyone is happy. But with my head bouncing around like a ping-pong ball lately, I’m starting to drop the ball on details I normally *never* miss. Like, I’ll completely overlook a client’s specific delivery note about where to leave the pallets, or I'll realize two days later that I completely forgot who I promised to call back at dispatch. It sounds small, maybe, but when you’re managing tight schedules and heavy loads, you just can’t be doing that. You lose trust. It's just this constant jumping around in my head, and I can't seem to filter the noise out anymore. So... yeah, that's what finally made me sit down in this chair today.
Have you noticed this kind of distractibility and difficulty focusing since you were a child or a teenager, or is this really a new change for you starting just in the past few months?

Oh, no, no. Definitely not since I was a kid. I mean, back in school, I wasn't exactly the valedictorian or anything, but I could always pay attention when I needed to. If I had a job to do, I did it. Same when I started driving in my twenties. You don't get a million safe miles under your belt if you've been distracted your whole life, you know? So, no, this is... this is definitely a new thing for me. 

If I really sit down and trace it back, I’d say it’s been going on for about seven months now. Yeah, right around seven months. Because that was exactly when my daughter moved back home with me. She, uh... well, she had a bit of a rough patch with her living situation, her lease ended, things were just up in the air for her. So of course I told her she could come back to her old room. You know how it is with your kids, no matter how old they get, you're always their dad, you always want to help them out and make sure they have a safe place to land. 

But man, having her back really shifted the dynamic at the house, and I suddenly found myself trying to juggle my freight routes, making sure she was getting back on her feet, managing the extra groceries and bills, and just... trying to keep everything steady, you know? I really wanted to be the rock for her. And I think right around then, when I started trying to keep the whole household locked down and steady so she wouldn't stress, that's when my brain just started doing this... this jumping around thing. I remember it was right after she brought the last of her boxes over, and I was trying to figure out where to put her extra furniture in the garage, and ever since then, it's just been this constant thing where I can't just focus on one simple task without ten other things cutting in line. So yeah, seven months, give or take.
Along with this racing, jumping mind, have you also noticed feeling unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, or needing much less sleep than usual and not feeling tired?

You know, it’s funny you use those exact words, because... well, yes. Absolutely yes to the mood stuff. For months now, I’ve been having these stretches where I am just so fired up. I mean, unbelievably fired up. I’ll be sitting up in the cab of my rig, looking out over the interstate, and I just get this overwhelming feeling that everything is going to work out perfectly, no matter what. Like, my daughter’s situation? Completely fine, it's all part of a master plan. My routes? Perfect. I even started drawing up plans to buy a second truck, maybe start my own mini-fleet, which is honestly a little crazy in this economy with fuel prices where they are, but in my head, I’m just like, "I can do this, I can conquer the world right now!" I get this huge buzz, this absolute certainty that I’m on top of everything and nothing can touch me. It’s like I’ve got this massive engine running inside my chest. 

But then... on the flip side of that, it’s like that exact same energy just curdles or turns sour somehow. I get so irritable. And I mean snapping over the smallest, most ridiculous stuff at home and out in the yard. Just the other weekend, I was out back trying to fix the latch on the side gate—the wood swelled up from all that rain we had a few weeks back, you know how that goes—and my daughter came out just to ask me a simple question about the Wi-Fi router acting up. Just a normal, everyday question. And I just snapped at her. Bit her head right off over absolutely nothing! Or if I'm out mowing the lawn and the mower sputters, or if I drop a wrench on the driveway, I just see red. 

And Doc, that is *not* my usual way. Not at all. I’m a patient guy. You have to be patient to haul eighty thousand pounds of freight through Chicago rush hour traffic, right? You can’t be a hothead out on the road. You just can't. But lately, for months now, it’s just this constant pendulum. I’m either flying high and thinking I'm invincible and the world is my oyster, or I’m barking at my kid over a garden hose being left out. It’s... it's really throwing me off, to be honest with you.

Before these past seven months, have you ever gone through a period—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually depressed, low, or lost interest in things, or a separate earlier time where you felt this same kind of high energy and racing thoughts?

Well, let me really think back on that... no. No, honestly, I haven't. I mean, as far as being depressed or feeling low goes, sure, life throws curveballs at you, right? Like when the freight industry took a massive hit back around '08, or just, you know, regular life stress... it was tough, and you worry about paying the bills and keeping the lights on, but I never got down in the dumps where I lost interest in things or couldn't get out of bed for a week. I’ve always been the kind of guy who just puts his work boots on, grabs his thermos, and gets the job done. You just keep pushing forward, you know? You have to. So no, never any of that dark cloud stuff where I just gave up on things. 

And as for the high energy or the racing mind before these last seven months? Definitely not. Like I was saying before, I’ve always prided myself on being steady. Just completely even-keeled. You wake up, you get your coffee—usually just a black coffee from whatever pilot station or truck stop is right off the interstate—you do your pre-trip inspection, check your air brakes, kick the tires, and you just drive. You put the miles in. I never had these big, wild ideas about buying up a whole fleet of trucks or feeling like I was invincible before. I was just a regular, predictable guy making an honest living. 

Honestly, Doc, you could practically set your watch by me for the last thirty years. I’d run my routes, come home, maybe tinker with a carburetor in the garage or watch a ballgame on the couch, and then just go to sleep. Simple as that. Never any of this bouncing off the walls or feeling like a superhero. So this whole... this whole rollercoaster I'm on right now with the buzzing energy and the snapping at my kid over the garden hose, it really is a brand new thing. It all just kicked off when she moved her boxes back into the house and I started trying to manage everything all at once. Before that? Just a straight line, steady as she goes.

During these periods when you're feeling on top of the world and full of big plans, have you ever experienced things like hearing voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or become so convinced of something—like your business plans being guaranteed to succeed—that no evidence or argument from others could change your mind?

Hearing voices? Oh, no, no, definitely nothing like that. I'm not hearing the CB radio when it's unplugged or people whispering in the garage or anything spooky like that. It’s always just my own voice in my head, it’s just... well, it's just going a million miles an hour, you know? 

But as far as getting totally convinced of things and not listening to anyone else? Yeah. Yeah, I’d say that hits the nail right on the head. Because, well, let me give you a perfect example of what I mean. Just a few weeks ago, I got it in my head that I could rebuild the whole driver training program myself. Our company has this whole onboarding thing for the rookies, right? The guys fresh out of CDL school who barely know how to float gears. And usually, I just do my job and let the safety guys handle the teaching, but suddenly I was just absolutely certain that I could overhaul the entire thing and make it run better than the bosses ever could. 

I mean, I was sitting at the kitchen table at two in the morning with a yellow legal pad, drawing out new road test routes, writing up new protocols for coupling trailers and checking air lines, and I was so convinced that this was going to revolutionize the whole company. I was ready to march into the terminal and demand a presentation. My daughter tried to tell me to slow down, she came into the kitchen and was like, "Dad, you drive the freight, you don't own the terminal, why are you doing this?" but I wouldn't hear a word of it. I just brushed her off. I thought she was just blind to how brilliant my plan was. I even cornered my dispatcher about it the next morning, telling him I needed a sit-down meeting with the regional manager because I had the golden ticket to fix all their efficiency problems. 

And the crazy thing is, Doc, that’s not really my lane. At all. I’ve been behind the wheel for thirty years, I just have a high school diploma, I’m not a corporate guy, and I sure as heck don't write training manuals for a living. But in that moment? You couldn't have told me I wasn't the smartest guy in the entire logistics industry. I was bulletproof. I knew I was right, and any evidence to the contrary was just people not seeing the big picture. So yeah, I definitely get locked into those big plans and just won't let go, even when people try to talk some sense into me.
